note: Night places that do not expire — things only on after dark, live rooms, jazz, comedy and cabaret, dancing, bars, night markets and late-night food. Researched, not visited: every record says so. Programmes change nightly, so the link goes to the venue's own calendar; dated concerts belong in events.json.

items.title: SFJAZZ Center
items.why: The first free-standing building in America built for jazz, open since 2013. The main hall seats 350 to 700 depending on the set-up, and nowhere in it is far from the stage. The programme runs from legends to local players. Pick a night from the calendar.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Black Cat
items.why: A jazz supper club downstairs in the Tenderloin: live sets most nights, cocktails, and dinner at candlelit tables. San Francisco Magazine called it the city's most romantic spot. Book a table for the early set.
items.source: Black Cat; OpenTable; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: blackcatsf.com

items.title: Punch Line
items.why: San Francisco's longest-running comedy club, open since 1978, and its only full-time one. Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Chris Rock worked out their acts here. The room is small enough that there are no bad seats.
items.source: Punch Line; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Cobb's Comedy Club
items.why: The bigger of the two stand-up rooms, in North Beach, where touring headliners play. Check the calendar, since who is on is the whole decision. Walk to Vesuvio afterwards.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: BATS Improv
items.why: Improv at the Bayfront Theatre in Fort Mason on Saturday nights, with a short early show at 6:45 and the main one at 8. It is unscripted and different every time, and cheap enough to take a chance on. Coffee at Equator by the gate first.
items.source: Fort Mason Center; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0
items.hoursNote: Main-stage shows on Saturday nights; improv.org has the season

items.title: The Fillmore
items.why: The ballroom where Bill Graham put on the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane and Big Brother between 1965 and 1968. The walls are still covered with the posters. Go for whoever is playing, and arrive early to read the walls.
items.source: The Fillmore; FoundSF; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Great American Music Hall
items.why: San Francisco's oldest nightclub, built in 1907 after the earthquake, with its gilded columns, carved balconies and original ceiling murals still in place. The room is as much the reason to go as the band.
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Vesuvio
items.area: 255 Columbus Avenue, on Jack Kerouac Alley
items.why: The Beats' bar, opened in 1948 across the alley from City Lights. Kerouac, Ginsberg and Neal Cassady drank here, and Cassady stopped in on his way to the Six Gallery reading in 1955. It is a museum you can drink in. Buy a book at City Lights, then take it upstairs here.
items.source: Wikipedia; vesuvio.com; National Trust for Historic Preservation; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/35537202)
items.hoursFrom: vesuvio.com

items.title: Tosca Cafe
items.why: Open since 1919, a red-leather room on Columbus. Order the house cappuccino, which isn't coffee at all but a Prohibition-era hot chocolate with bourbon and cognac. It was saved from closing and reopened with dinner. Go late and sit at the bar.
items.source: Tosca Cafe; SF Chronicle; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: toscacafe-sf.com

items.title: Li Po Cocktail Lounge
items.why: Chinatown's oldest bar, open since 1937 and barely changed: red lanterns, a low ceiling and a Buddha shrine behind the bar. Order the Chinese mai tai. The recipe is a secret and uses a Chinese liqueur they make themselves.
items.hoursFrom: the Corner and SF Station listings

items.title: Smuggler's Cove
items.why: A three-storey tiki bar with more rums than any other bar in the country, over thirteen hundred. There are eighty cocktails on the menu, and it was named the best cocktail bar in the United States in 2016. Martin Cate, who founded it in 2009, wrote the book on rum. Go early, because it is small and the line forms.
items.source: Wikipedia; PUNCH; World's 50 Best; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: smugglerscovesf.com

items.title: Trick Dog
items.why: The Mission cocktail bar that reinvents its whole menu around a theme every so often: a wrestling belt one year, a book of San Francisco photographs the next. It won the cocktail world's top award in 2025. Order off whatever the current menu is.
items.source: SF Standard; Axios; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: trickdogbar.com

items.title: Zam Zam
items.why: A 1941 Persian Art Deco cocktail lounge in the Haight, opened as the Persian Aub Zam Zam, with arches and murals. For decades its owner famously ran it with an iron hand. Order a martini, which is what it is known for.
items.source: SF Heritage; SF Examiner; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: the Yelp and Tripadvisor listings — Zam Zam has no website

items.title: The Rose & Crown
items.why: Palo Alto's oldest bar, an English pub on Emerson with more than twenty beers on tap, and fish and chips. Tuesday is trivia night: claim a table between 7:30 and 7:50, and the winners drink for free.
items.source: Palo Alto Online; confirmed against OpenStreetMap (way/133116331)
items.hoursFrom: therosepa.com

items.title: Dutch Goose
items.area: 3567 Alameda de las Pulgas, Menlo Park
items.why: The Stanford crowd's bar since 1966: peanut shells on the floor, burgers, pitchers, and deviled eggs made to the same recipe for sixty years. Order the eggs.
items.source: Stanford Magazine; M-A Chronicle; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: dutchgoose.net

items.title: British Bankers Club
items.why: A 1925 brick building by Birge Clark that has been a bank, Menlo Park's city hall and its jail. It has been a bar since 1977, now with a rooftop. Drink on the roof on a warm evening.
items.source: The Almanac; InMenlo; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursFrom: britishbankersclub.com

items.title: Frost Amphitheater
items.why: An outdoor bowl on the Stanford campus, from 1937, where 8,000 people sit on grass slopes above the stage. The summer and autumn concerts are the Peninsula's best big night out. Bring a blanket and a layer.
items.source: Stanford Live; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Bob Aronson from Monterey, CA, US · CC BY-SA 2.0
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Bing Concert Hall
items.why: Stanford's concert hall, open since 2013: 842 seats in vineyard-style terraces around the stage, with acoustics by Yasuhisa Toyota. Stanford Live puts on classical, jazz and world music here. Every seat is close.
items.source: Stanford Live; Wikipedia; confirmed against OpenStreetMap
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable

items.title: Exploratorium After Dark
items.hoursFrom: exploratorium.edu — After Dark, Thursdays 6 to 10pm, last entry 8:30
items.why: The science museum on Pier 15 with the children gone and a bar open. Every Thursday from six it is adults only, and the hundreds of hands-on exhibits are yours, down to the glass-walled observatory gallery over the bay. Each night has a theme and a talk or a DJ. It is the best first date in the city. Buy tickets ahead and arrive by eight, because last entry is 8:30.

items.title: NightLife at the Academy of Sciences
items.area: 55 Music Concourse Drive, Golden Gate Park
items.hoursFrom: calacademy.org — NightLife, Thursdays 6 to 10pm, 21+
items.why: Thursday nights in Golden Gate Park: a four-storey rainforest under a glass dome, a coral reef, the penguins, and DJs and bars between them. It is 21 and over, so bring physical ID. Planetarium seats cost a few dollars more and go first, so reserve them with the ticket. Eat before you come or after; the park is dark and quiet by ten.

items.title: Audium
items.hoursFrom: audium.org — performances Thursday, Friday and Saturday at 8pm, doors 7:30
items.why: The only theatre of its kind in the world: forty-nine seats in a sloping room with 176 speakers in the walls, floor and ceiling, and the lights go out completely. Sound moves past you, over you and under you for about an hour. Stan Shaff began it in the late 1960s, and his son David now performs the pieces. Three nights a week at eight. Some tickets are sold in advance and a few pay-what-you-can seats go at the door from 7:30.

items.title: The Bay Lights
items.area: Best from Pier 14 or Pier 7, the Embarcadero
items.hoursFrom: illuminate.org — the lights run nightly from dusk to dawn
items.why: Forty-eight thousand LEDs on the cables of the Bay Bridge's western span, running patterns that never repeat. The piece went dark in 2023 and was relit on 20 March 2026, with a second strand added so it can be seen from more of the shore. Walk out to the end of Pier 14 or Pier 7 after sunset. It pairs with dinner at the Ferry Building, a ten-minute walk away.
items.imageSubject: The Bay Lights on the Bay Bridge

items.title: Telescope nights at Chabot
items.hoursFrom: chabotspace.org — free telescope viewings Friday and Saturday, 7:30 to 10:30pm
items.source: Chabot Space & Science Center; NASA Night Sky Network
items.why: Every Friday and Saturday night the observatory domes in the Oakland hills open for free, and you look through real telescopes: a refractor from 1883 named Leah, a 20-inch from 1916 named Rachel, and a 36-inch reflector. Volunteer astronomers point each one at something different and answer questions. If it is cloudy the domes are still open to tour; if it rains, stay home. Bring a layer: it is up in the redwoods.
items.firstStep: Free, no ticket — go round the back to the Observatory Deck

items.title: Castro Theatre
items.hoursNote: Open for shows and screenings — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The 1922 movie palace under the neon sign, reopened on 6 February 2026 after a two-year, $41 million restoration. Another Planet now runs it for concerts, films, drag and comedy, with 1,400 seats that can be taken out for standing shows. The ceiling and the Wurlitzer organ are the reasons to go whatever is on. Frameline, the LGBTQ+ film festival, is here every June.

items.title: Bimbo's 365 Club
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A 1931 supper club at the top of Columbus, still run by the family that opened it, and still one of the best-looking rooms a band can play in this city. The bookings run from indie bands to swing orchestras. It is a ten-minute walk up from Washington Square, and small enough that you will see the stage from anywhere.

items.title: The Independent
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The room where bands play San Francisco on the way up: about five hundred standing, good sound, and nowhere far from the stage. Check the calendar a month out, because the names you will know next year sell it out. Divisadero is full of places to eat before a show, and the doors are usually at seven or eight.

items.title: Bottom of the Hill
items.hoursNote: Open for shows — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A small rock club at the foot of Potrero Hill, open since 1991, where three bands a night play for a few hundred people and the ticket costs less than a cocktail downtown. A lot of bands that went on to fill arenas played here first. There is a patio out the back for between sets.

items.title: Shoreline Amphitheatre
items.priceNote: Lawn seats are the cheap way in
items.hoursNote: Open for shows, roughly April to October — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The Peninsula's big outdoor stage: 22,000 people under a white tent roof and on a grass lawn by the bay in Mountain View. The season runs from spring into October, and this is where the arena tours stop. Buy a lawn ticket and bring a blanket. Leaving takes as long as the encore, so park facing the exit or cycle in on the Stevens Creek Trail.

items.title: Keys Jazz Bistro
items.hoursFrom: keysjazzbistro.com — Wednesday to Saturday, 5pm to 1am; sets at 7 and 9, and 11 on Saturday
items.why: Jazz back on Broadway, in a 125-seat room built around a Yamaha grand and a Hammond B3 organ. Sets are at seven and nine, with a late one at eleven on Saturday, and dinner is served at the tables. The booking leans to piano, organ trios and singers. It is all-ages, which almost no jazz room is, and two minutes from Vesuvio.

items.title: Dear San Francisco at Club Fugazi
items.hoursNote: Shows most evenings plus weekend matinées — check the calendar
items.why: A hundred minutes of circus about San Francisco, in the North Beach hall where Beach Blanket Babylon played for forty-five years. It is made by The 7 Fingers, whose founders grew up here: acrobats on poles and hoops a few feet from the front row, telling the city's story from the gold rush to now. Wine and small plates are sold inside. It is the best thing to take visitors to, and good without them.

items.title: Oasis
items.hoursNote: Open for shows and parties — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: San Francisco's drag cabaret, in a converted bathhouse on 11th Street, run by D'Arcy Drollinger since 2015. It nearly closed in 2025. A donation let it buy the building, and it reopened on 17 July 2026 with a new gold-tiled box office and pink curtains. There are staged shows early in the evening and dance parties after, and the full-length drag parodies of films and TV sell out first.

items.title: Rooster T. Feathers
items.hoursNote: Shows most nights — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: Silicon Valley's comedy club since 1984, on El Camino in Sunnyvale: a low-ceilinged room of small tables where touring headliners work out their hour. It is the one real stand-up room south of the city, so from Palo Alto it is fifteen minutes rather than an hour. Everyone is 21 and over, so bring ID, and buy tickets from the club's own site.

items.title: Public Works
items.hoursNote: Open for club nights, usually Thursday to Saturday from about 9:30pm — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The city's serious dance floor: two rooms down an alley off Mission Street, a Funktion-One sound system, and house and techno DJs from Berlin, Detroit and the Bay on the same bill. It runs by the calendar rather than by the week, so check who is on. Nights start around half past nine and go late.

items.title: The EndUp
items.hoursNote: Open Thursday to Sunday; the Saturday party runs through Sunday morning — check the listings
items.why: The after-hours club, at the corner of 6th and Harrison since 1973. On Saturday night it keeps going through Sunday morning, and the point is walking out onto the garden patio into daylight. Everybody who stayed up too late in San Francisco for fifty years has ended up here. Go after one in the morning, never before.

items.title: El Rio
items.priceNote: Cheap · some nights have a cover
items.hoursNote: Open daily; Salsa Sunday on the second and fourth Sunday from 3pm
items.source: SF Legacy Business Registry; SF Station
items.why: A queer bar in the outer Mission since 1978, with one of the best back patios in the city: lemon trees, string lights and heaters, and room for a band and a crowd dancing. On the second and fourth Sunday of the month Salsa Sunday starts at three, with live salsa, merengue and cumbia bands. The rest of the week it is drag, karaoke, comedy and dance parties. The city has protected the patio as part of its Legacy Business listing.

items.title: Church of 8 Wheels
items.hoursFrom: churchof8wheels.com — adult sessions Friday and Saturday, 7 to 11pm
items.why: Roller disco in a deconsecrated church: a skating floor under the stained glass, a DJ and a disco ball. The Friday and Saturday evening sessions, seven to eleven, are for adults. Twenty dollars cash covers the skates. Nobody here is good at it, which is the point.

items.title: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
items.area: Fairmont Hotel, 950 Mason Street, Nob Hill
items.priceNote: Cocktails ~$20 · cover when the band plays
items.hoursFrom: fairmont-san-francisco.com — Wednesday and Thursday 5 to 10pm, Friday and Saturday 5 to 11pm
items.why: A tiki bar built in 1945 in the Fairmont's old swimming pool. The pool is now a lagoon, a band plays top-forty covers from a thatched barge on it from seven, and every half hour or so a tropical storm rolls through, with thunder, lightning and rain on the water. It is absurd and everyone should go once.

items.title: Top of the Mark
items.area: 19th floor, Mark Hopkins Hotel, Nob Hill
items.priceNote: Cocktails ~$20 · $15 cover for the Saturday band
items.hoursFrom: topofthemark.com — Sunday to Thursday 4 to 11pm, Friday and Saturday 3pm to 12:30am
items.why: The glass-walled bar on the nineteenth floor of the Mark Hopkins, open since 1939, where sailors shipping out in the Second World War had a last drink looking at the Golden Gate. The view goes all the way round: the bridge, the bay, the Financial District lit up. There is a band on Saturday nights. Come at sunset and take the window seats on the north side.

items.title: Specs'
items.hoursFrom: specsbarsf.com — daily from 4pm, to 2am Thursday to Saturday
items.source: Specs' Twelve Adler Museum Cafe; Wikipedia
items.why: A North Beach bar down a dead-end alley across Columbus from Vesuvio, open since 1968 and full of things sailors and regulars brought back: whale bones, walrus tusks, flags, and a case of oddities by the door. It is dim and argumentative, the way a bar used to be. Order a beer. Ask about anything on the walls.

items.title: Bourbon & Branch
items.hoursFrom: bourbonandbranch.com — 6pm to midnight Sunday to Wednesday, to 2am Thursday to Saturday
items.why: The speakeasy that started San Francisco's cocktail revival in 2006, behind an unmarked door on a Prohibition-era site. Book the main bar and you are sent a password for the night. The Library, at the back, takes walk-ins. The menu is long and the bartenders will make you something off it if you tell them what you like.

items.title: The Mint
items.priceNote: Drinks · a small tip per song
items.hoursFrom: The Mint — 5pm to 2am, from 4pm at weekends, closed Tuesday
items.why: The city's karaoke bar, singing since 1993. There are no private rooms: you sing to the whole bar from a proper stage, and the whole bar cheers. The book has 25,000 songs. Put your name down early, because by eleven on a Friday the wait is an hour. It is closed on Tuesdays.

items.title: The Patio
items.hoursNote: Opens at 11am every day and runs late at weekends — check the closing time before a late night
items.why: Downtown Palo Alto's outdoor bar: three open-air yards, the longest bar in town, and twenty-odd screens for whatever game is on. There is karaoke and trivia in the week. It is not a cocktail bar and does not pretend to be. It is where the Peninsula goes when it wants a loud night without driving to the city.

items.title: Chinatown Night Market
items.area: Grant Avenue and Waverly Place, Chinatown
items.priceNote: Free to walk; food from the stalls
items.hoursNote: Second Friday of the month, May to October, 5 to 9pm — the last of 2026 is 9 October
items.source: SF Funcheap; San Francisco Chinatown Merchants
items.why: Five blocks of Grant Avenue closed to cars on one Friday a month: street food, lion dancers, beer and wine gardens, and the shops staying open under the lanterns. It runs from five to nine, May to October, and 9 October is the last one this year. Start at the Dragon Gate on Bush and walk north, then finish with a mai tai at Li Po.

items.title: Fort Mason Night Market
items.area: Fort Mason Center, on the waterfront
items.hoursNote: One Friday a month, May to December, 5 to 10pm — next on 16 October, 6 November and 18 December
items.source: Fort Mason Center; Off the Grid; SF Funcheap
items.why: The old army piers on the Marina waterfront on a Friday night: a hundred-odd stalls of food trucks, makers and vintage, live music, and the Golden Gate going dark at the end of the quay. It is free and runs from five to ten on one Friday a month. The rest of 2026 is 16 October, 6 November and a holiday market on 18 December. Eat from the trucks, then have a drink at The Interval by the gate.
items.imageCredit: Original uploader was SuperJumbo at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

items.title: El Farolito
items.hoursFrom: elfarolitosf.com — daily to 2:45am, to 3:45am Friday and Saturday
items.why: The Mission burrito the city argues about, and the answer at two in the morning: open until 2:45 every night and 3:45 on Fridays and Saturdays. Order the super carne asada burrito, or the quesadilla suiza if you know. There are fluorescent lights and a queue out of the door after the bars shut, and it is right by the 24th Street BART.

items.title: Bob's Donuts
items.hoursFrom: bobsdonutssf.com — open 24 hours on Polk Street
items.why: A doughnut shop open twenty-four hours, where the fryers never stop and the apple fritter is the size of your face. It moved a few doors up Polk to 1720 but kept the hours, and at three in the morning it is the only warm, lit room on the street. There is a giant doughnut you can try to eat in under three minutes, if the night has gone that way.

items.title: Zareen's
items.hoursFrom: KQED; zareensrestaurant.com — daily 11am to midnight, takeout only after 11pm
items.why: Pakistani and Indian home cooking on California Avenue, and the rare Palo Alto kitchen still going at midnight, every night. It is the only one of Zareen's three restaurants that stays open late. Order the chicken tikka masala and the chapli kebab. It is takeout only after eleven, so eat in before then.

items.title: The Guild Theatre
items.hoursNote: Open for shows, doors usually 7pm and music at 8 — the calendar is the timetable
items.source: The Guild Theatre; The Almanac; Cinema Treasures
items.why: Menlo Park’s 1926 cinema, rebuilt inside its old walls and reopened in 2022 as a live-music room run by a non-profit. It holds about 500 standing or 200 seated, so touring bands that fill much bigger halls elsewhere play here at arm’s length. It is on El Camino, so from Palo Alto you are home ten minutes after the encore.

items.title: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
items.hoursNote: Open for performances — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: Three stages at the top of Castro Street: a 600-seat MainStage, a 200-seat SecondStage and the ParkStage. TheatreWorks Silicon Valley and Peninsula Youth Theatre are the resident companies, and dance, choirs, music and family shows fill the rest of the calendar. Dinner on Castro first and you walk to your seat.
items.imageSubject: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts

items.title: Open Mic Monday at Red Rock Coffee
items.area: Red Rock Coffee, 201 Castro Street, Mountain View (upstairs)
items.times: Every Monday, 6 to 9.30pm upstairs; lottery sign-ups 5.45 to 8pm. None on 28 December
items.firstStep: Put your name in the jar from 5.45pm for a five-minute set, or just come and listen
items.hoursNote: Every Monday, 6 to 9.30pm; sign-ups 5.45 to 8pm. None on 28 December
items.why: One of the Bay Area’s longest-running open mics, upstairs in a Castro Street coffee house every Monday night. Musicians, poets and comics draw five-minute slots by lottery, so nobody needs to queue early. It is kept family-friendly and has no age limit, so it works as a school-night outing with a teenager who plays. Go twice and you will start recognising the regulars.
items.imageSubject: Castro and Villa, the corner Red Rock Coffee stands on

items.title: Club Fox Blues Jam
items.times: Every Wednesday from 7pm: a featured band, then the jam
items.hoursNote: Every Wednesday from 7pm
items.why: A Wednesday-night blues jam that turned twenty in 2026, in the cabaret room beside Redwood City’s Fox Theatre. A regional or touring rhythm-and-blues band plays a set, then local players take the stage in turns. There are tables and a dance floor. It is the Peninsula’s steadiest weekly night of live music.
items.imageSubject: The Fox Theatre, next door on Broadway

items.title: Meyhouse Jazz
items.priceNote: Ticket for the show; dinner and drinks charged separately
items.cadence: Most Fridays and Saturdays, two seatings
items.times: Seatings at 5pm (show around 6:30) and 8pm (show around 8:30); each set runs about 75 minutes
items.hoursNote: Most Friday and Saturday nights; seatings at 5pm and 8pm
items.why: On most Friday and Saturday nights the Turkish restaurant on Emerson becomes a jazz supper club. The chef-owner books the music himself: touring trios and quartets, singers working through a songbook, and the odd classical Sunday. There are two seatings, at five and at eight, each with a set of about an hour and a quarter, and you eat meze while the band plays. Buy the ticket ahead; food and drink go on a separate bill. Along with the Club Fox jam, it is one of the few regular live rooms on the Peninsula.

items.title: Band Jam Night at The Hub
items.times: Every Tuesday, 8.30 to 10.30pm, on the upstairs stage
items.firstStep: Bring your instrument; the drums, keyboard and PA are there
items.hoursNote: Every Tuesday, 8.30 to 10.30pm
items.why: A standing Tuesday jam on a proper upstairs stage, with a full PA, drum kit and keyboard. You bring a guitar or a horn and join in with whoever turned up. There is no cover, and it is 21 and over. It is the place for the parent who used to be in a band.
